draft.title: Business in the economy
card: Businesses employ people. Wages and salaries give households incomes, which they spend on goods and services.
Businesses pay taxes, such as company tax, to the government. The government uses tax revenue to fund services like schools, hospitals and roads.
Business output is the goods and services it produces. Together, this output adds to the economy and can raise living standards, meaning how well people live.
Business can also harm quality of life. A factory that pollutes a river is one example.
draft.remember: Business creates jobs, tax revenue and output, but can also cause harm such as pollution.

a.q: Which of these is a way a business supports government services?
opts: It pays tax, which the government spends on services
It pays wages, which households spend in shops
It produces goods, which customers can own
It cuts expenses, which raises its profit
a.why: Tax paid by businesses becomes government revenue, which funds services such as schools and hospitals. Wages give households income, but that is a link to jobs and incomes, not to government services.
a.clue: Which option sends money to the government?

b.q: Dana's bakery in Bathurst hires six staff and pays company tax. A nearby resident says its night-time ovens and delivery vans are noisy. Which statement about the bakery is correct?
opts: It gives jobs and tax revenue but can reduce quality of life
It adds to living standards only, as jobs outweigh the noise
It harms quality of life only, as noise is the main effect
It has no effect on the economy because it is small
b.why: The bakery provides jobs and incomes and pays tax, so it contributes to the economy. The noise is still a cost to nearby residents, so both effects exist. Saying jobs cancel the noise is tempting, but the card shows business can help and harm at once.
b.clue: A business can have good and bad effects at the same time.

a.best: It pays tax, which the government spends on services

b.best: It gives jobs and tax revenue but can reduce quality of life

problems.detail: The clue 'Which option sends money to the government?' points straight at the correct option and gives the answer away.
